title: "Palace Electrostatic + SGB"
---

::: {.callout-note title="CONVERGING candidate contract"}
The backend, Route A/B lowering, handoff, Slurm execution, strict result
resolution, and report summaries have live candidate evidence. They remain
CONVERGING and are not V1 stable.
:::

## Candidate surface

The public backend object is `scgsim.palace.ElectrostaticSim`. Staged calls
expose geometry, terminals, solver configuration, mesh, config, handoff, and
result processing instead of hiding the workflow in one orchestration cell.

The intended visible sequence is:

```text
construct component
-> set geometry / stack / airbox
-> add exact-net terminals
-> configure Electrostatic
-> mesh / config
-> common handoff
-> resolve / results / report
```

Handoff preparation does not submit Palace. Generated local or Slurm scripts
execute explicitly and write a receipt that the resolver verifies. Slurm
scripts bind `#SBATCH --output` and `--error` to `logs/palace-%j.log` so the
scheduler does not also write `slurm-%j.out`.

| Stage | Candidate method | Intended responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Geometry input | `set_geometry` | Bind the public Component input to the SGB geometry route. |
| Stack input | `set_stack` | Bind the layer-stack input consumed by SGB. |
| Airbox | `set_airbox` | Declare the simulation-domain envelope before geometry production. |
| Terminal binding | `add_terminal` | Select a terminal by exact SGB net identity. |
| Problem controls | `set_electrostatic` | Declare Electrostatic-specific config controls. |
| Output identity | `set_output_dir` | Bind the mesh/config/handoff output location. |
| Mesh | `mesh` | Request the SGB-backed Palace mesh path. |
| Config | `write_config` | Write the Palace Electrostatic configuration for the reviewed mesh identities. |

These methods are reachable candidate APIs.

## SGB and Palace ownership

SGB is the only semantic geometry and topology authority. The first
implementation route is Route B:

```text
Component + layer stack
-> SGB XAO and structured physical-group records
-> Palace mesh and config
```

Route A follows through the same pipeline; it is not a second runner or
topology system. SCGSim owns only Palace-specific lowering, mesh/config,
handoff, resolve, and report behavior built on SGB identities.

The candidate has no native-geometry fallback, physical-name semantic parsing,
replacement topology reconstruction, or external gdsfactory/cloud execution
fallback. Terminal selection is exact SGB net identity; legacy center/name
inference remains outside the contract.

## Candidate Electrostatic defaults

These values are **CONVERGING**, not accepted scientific defaults or Gates:

| Control | Candidate value |
|---|---|
| `save_fields` | `0` |
| `unassigned_conductor_policy` | `"ground"` |
| `exterior_boundary_policy` | `"none"` |
| `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal` | `false` unless the notebook sets `amr_nonconformal=True` |

Palace defaults `Nonconformal` to `true` when the key is omitted. SCGSim always
writes the key and defaults it to `false` (conformal tet AMR). Notebooks opt
into nonconformal AMR with `set_numerical(amr_nonconformal=True)`.

External gsim and historical SGB revisions are derivation evidence only. The
runtime authority is the in-tree `scgsim.sgb` Core and the current
`scgsim.palace` implementation.

See [Geometry and SGB Route A/B](../geometry-sgb.qmd),
[Execution Profiles and Local/Manual-HPC Handoff](../execution-profiles.qmd),
and [Provenance and Data Boundaries](../provenance.qmd) for the surrounding
contracts.
